placement.rationale: The preemptible h100-1x pool that carried the original one-off Mosaic qualification is at zero nodes for this campaign. Only the two always-hot capacity-block nodes advertise H100 GPUs, so every trial is pinned to the reserved-8x flavor that Kueue actually covers.

boundaries.start: the instant the Pod is scheduled onto a Ready accelerator node, which is the capacity-available point for a batch stage
boundaries.end: the first semantic result the model emits, which for a batch runtime is the same instant as semantic ready

level_contract.boundary_rationale: The published contract assigns queue admission and placement to capacity wait, and assigns image setup, artifact restore, runtime initialisation, weight transfer and compilation to model start. Sandbox and volume setup therefore counts inside model start, not outside it. Measuring from container start instead would silently hide the recursive volume-ownership pass, which the baseline trials showed is the single largest contributor.
level_contract.note: Capacity wait and Kueue queue wait are reported separately and are deliberately excluded from the level evaluation, exactly as the published contract requires.

fsgroup_recursive_ownership.startup_cost: 153-305 s per Pod start on a 128 GiB shared claim under the default fsGroupChangePolicy Always
fsgroup_recursive_ownership.remediation: fsGroupChangePolicy OnRootMismatch reduces it to 1-2 s
fsgroup_recursive_ownership.second_failure_mode: the same recursive pass rewrites ownership on the claim it walks. On the tenant-private academic claim it replaced the contract group 65532 with 10001 and made licensed bytes group-writable, leaving the parameter object unreadable to every contract-conforming Pod. The cost is a performance problem; the ownership rewrite is a correctness and licensing problem.
fsgroup_recursive_ownership.guidance: a Pod that only reads a shared claim should use supplementalGroups and set no fsGroup at all

external_artifacts.note: the runtime checks directory presence; the archive identity is pinned in the image lock

baseline.label: prepared-node, cold XLA compilation
baseline.description: The image and every external checkpoint are already resident on the node and on the regional shared filesystem, but the JAX persistent compilation cache lives in the per-Pod /tmp emptyDir, so each trial recompiles every XLA executable. This is the currently deployed truth.

warm-jit.label: prepared-node, ownership remediated, persistent XLA compilation cache
warm-jit.description: Carries the fsGroupChangePolicy OnRootMismatch remediation proven by the fast-volume cohort, so the recursive volume-ownership pass no longer masks anything, and additionally redirects the JAX persistent compilation cache to the regional shared filesystem so compiled XLA executables survive the Pod. This isolates the XLA compilation contribution to model start, which the fast-volume cohort left as Mosaic's remaining floor.
warm-jit.sequencing: Trial 1 runs alone and populates the shared compilation cache, so it pays the one-time compilation. Trials 2 to 4 run concurrently against the populated cache and form the steady-state cohort. Running all trials at once would make every one of them miss the cache and race to write it, which would measure nothing.
warm-jit.one_time_vs_steady_evidence: Compilation reuse is read from the runtime's own first-step timing rather than declared: the baseline cohort's first optimizer step took 87.61 s including JAX compilation against a steady 0.25 s per step, so a warm trial is one whose first step collapses toward the steady step time. The cache directory's entry count and byte size are probed on the claim before and after the cohort as corroboration.
warm-jit.threshold_finding: The first attempt used JAX_PERSISTENT_CACHE_MIN_COMPILE_TIME_SECS=0.5 and cached nothing at all: the cache directory was never created and the first optimizer step still took 85.88 s. Mosaic's startup is not one long compilation but many short ones, so every module fell under the 0.5 s floor and JAX skipped the write silently. The floor is now 0. This is the failure mode a fast-start mechanism can have while looking configured, which is why the campaign probes the cache directory instead of trusting the setting.

mechanism_preflight.claim: JAX persistent compilation caching is available in this image on the CUDA backend
mechanism_preflight.evidence: probe Pod fsc-jax-gpu-cache-probe, same image digest, one H100, wrote 5 cache entries including xla_gpu_per_fusion_autotune_cache_dir after a 1.50 s compile with the floor at 0
mechanism_preflight.cpu_control: probe Pod fsc-jax-cache-probe on the CPU backend wrote 2 entries, confirming the env binding itself

jit_cache_evidence.probe: faststart.py probe-cache, a short-lived read-only Pod that counts files and bytes on the claim
jit_cache_evidence.meaning: trial 1 ran against an empty cache and populated it; trials 2 to 4 ran against those 2103 entries

fast-volume.label: prepared-node, no recursive volume ownership pass
fast-volume.description: Identical to baseline except fsGroupChangePolicy is OnRootMismatch. The default Always policy makes the kubelet walk and chown the entire shared artifact volume on every Pod start, which the baseline trials showed dominates model start. OnRootMismatch skips the walk when the volume root already carries the target group.

boltzgen.lane: optimized fused-kernel (cuEquivariance) lane; the portable no-kernel lane sha256:e2bb0a15c7585916ed650e851903bfe55643141f6521e36cdcb382670c0d3c02 is a separate runtime and is deliberately not collapsed into this one
boltzgen.argv_provenance: byte-identical to the argv recorded for job fs2-model-forward-boltzgen-optimized-v1-20260903 in the owning task's h100-qualification-receipt.json, except for the per-trial --output directory
boltzgen.container_security_deviation: readOnlyRootFilesystem is false for this runtime. Unlike the Mosaic image, the BoltzGen image was never hardened against a read-only root, and this campaign measures startup rather than auditing the hardening contract. Every writable path the runtime actually uses is still an explicit mount, and the shared artifact plane stays mounted read-only.

warm-cache.label: prepared-node, persistent kernel and compile caches
warm-cache.description: Identical to baseline except the kernel/compile caches are redirected to a campaign-owned directory on the regional shared filesystem, so trials after the first reuse compiled fused kernels. This isolates the kernel-compilation contribution to model start.

The default Always policy makes the kubelet walk and chown the entire shared artifact volume on every Pod start, which the baseline trials showed dominates model start. OnRootMismatch skips the walk when the volume root already carries the target group.

alphafold3.image_provenance: resolved from the live node image cache on the H100 capacity-block node, because every committed file redacts the registry path to "withheld". This is the digest the owning task recorded as historical-semantic-evidence; the unpublished clean-wrapper successor has a null digest and is deliberately not used.
alphafold3.kueue_note: The ClusterQueue inference-accelerators selects only namespace fs2-models, and the AlphaFold 3 parameter claim is tenant-private to fs2-academic-poc. A cross-namespace claim mount is impossible, so this model schedules directly against the accelerator pool exactly as its original semantic evidence Job did, and its GPU is therefore outside Kueue quota rather than borrowed from it.
alphafold3.argv_provenance: the inference argv recorded for job academic-af3-v304-semantic-v1, which is the official no-data-pipeline path; --norun_data_pipeline is what makes the unpublished reference-database bundle irrelevant to this measurement
alphafold3.pod_security_note: fsGroup is deliberately absent. The academic claim is group-owned by GID 65532 with 0440 files and 0550 directories, so access comes from a supplemental group; setting fsGroup would attempt a recursive ownership change on a read-only licensed tree.
